meta.name: MIT 6.0001 Lecture 1 — What is Computation?
meta.subject: Computer Science / Python
meta.description: Drills core ideas from MIT 6.0001 Lecture 1: computation, declarative vs imperative knowledge, what an algorithm needs, language aspects (syntax/static semantics/semantics), and Python basics (types, casting, operators, printing, bindings).

inputs.label: Fundamentally, a computer does two things. Pick the best pair:
options: understands goals and fills in missing steps
learns meanings from context like English
decides what you meant and fixes your code

inputs.label: Pick the statement that matches the lecture:
options: computers only do what you tell them to do
computers know what you mean even if you say it wrong
computers infer intent from context like English

inputs.label: Is the example declarative knowledge or imperative knowledge?
A 'recipe' becomes an algorithm when it has:
options: sequence of simple steps + flow of control + a way to stop

inputs.label: Which aspect of languages is being highlighted?
In lecture terms, what kind of issue is this?
What does the program print? (Type what appears in the console.)
What is the type of the printed value?

perField.fundamentals: From the lecture: computation = performs calculations + remembers results.
perField.explicit: Key phrase: computers only know/do what you tell them to do.
perField.knowledge_kind: Declarative = statement of fact. Imperative = recipe/how-to steps. Example: {{knowledgeExample}}
perField.algorithm_parts: Algorithm = 1) simple steps 2) flow of control 3) a way to stop.
perField.aspect: Syntax = form. Static semantics = which syntactically valid strings have meaning. Semantics = meaning. Primitive constructs = basic building blocks.
perField.error_type: Syntax error = illegal form. Static semantic error = legal form but meaningless (e.g., 3 + "hi"). 'Valid but different than intended' = program runs but not what you meant.
perField.printed: Mentally run the code. Reminders: / always yields a float; int(3.9) truncates; % gives remainder; ** is power.
perField.printed_type: Type rules: ints are whole numbers; floats have decimals; True/False are bool; None is NoneType.
